evidence.intree_statement: Definition extract {x : C} : W x ~> x := @ret (C^op) (W^op) H x.   (* the counit epsilon : W => Id, componentwise *)
Definition duplicate {x : C} : W x ~> W (W x) := @join (C^op) (W^op) H x.   (* the comultiplication delta : W => W o W *)
Lemma extract_duplicate {x : C} : extract ∘ duplicate ≈ id[W x].   (* counit law epsilon_W . delta = id *)
Lemma fmap_extract_duplicate {x : C} : fmap[W] extract ∘ duplicate ≈ id[W x].   (* counit law W epsilon . delta = id *)
Lemma duplicate_duplicate {x : C} : duplicate ∘ @duplicate x ≈ fmap[W] duplicate ∘ @duplicate x.   (* coassociativity delta_W . delta = W delta . delta *)

statement_record.book: A comonad L = <L, eps, delta> in a category A is an endofunctor L : A -> A with natural transformations eps : L -> Id_A (counit) and delta : L -> L^2 (comultiplication) satisfying coassociativity (delta L).delta = (L delta).delta : L -> L^3 and the counit laws (eps L).delta = 1_L = (L eps).delta : L -> L. Equivalently, a comonoid in the strict monoidal category A^A of endofunctors under composition; the formal dual of a monad (VI.1).
statement_record.intree: Definition Comonad `{M : C ⟶ C} := @Monad (C^op) (M^op). (Theory/Monad.v:144), with the covariant API in Comonad/Core.v: extract (counit, :131), duplicate (comultiplication L x ~> W(W x), :135), extract_duplicate : extract ∘ duplicate ≈ id (:160), fmap_extract_duplicate : fmap[W] extract ∘ duplicate ≈ id (:164), duplicate_duplicate : duplicate ∘ duplicate ≈ fmap[W] duplicate ∘ duplicate (coassociativity, :169), plus naturality of extract/duplicate (:149, :155).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The library realizes Mac Lane's 'formal dual of a monad' characterization definitionally (Comonad := Monad on the opposite category, so C^op^op = C by reflexivity and every comonad law IS the corresponding monad law read backwards), and exposes exactly the counit + comultiplication + coassociativity + both counit laws Mac Lane lists as equations (1). Setoid rephrasing (≈ for =) is faithful. The 'comonoid in A^A' characterization Mac Lane gives as equivalent is also available in-tree by duality from 'a monad is a monoid in [C,C]' (Theory/Monad.v:15,55; Monad/Monoid.v). If anything the in-tree development is stronger (adds extend/co-Kleisli laws), but the definitional core matches exactly.

verifier.notes: PRESENT verified at every cited location by direct read. Theory/Monad.v:144 (exact, confirmed by grep -n): Definition Comonad `{M : C ⟶ C} := @Monad (C^op) (M^op). Comonad/Core.v: extract:131, duplicate:135, extract_duplicate:160, fmap_extract_duplicate:164, duplicate_duplicate:169 -- all code quotes exact (the trailing (* ... *) annotations in the evidence are the classifier's gloss, but each precisely matches the preceding docstring at :130/:133/:159/:163/:167). Both counit laws AND coassociativity are present; naturality of extract (:149) and duplicate (:155) also present, so eps and delta are genuine natural transformations. Matches Mac Lane eqs (1) exactly. Both files registered in _CoqProject (Comonad/Core.v line 14, Theory/Monad.v line 461). strength_comparison 'same' is honest.
